description:
scripts/research-os/paging-allowlist.ts keys each exception by `path:line` as paging-scan reports it. Every edit above a listed read shifts the key, and the gate then reports the read as unlisted and the entry as stale. It happened twice on 2026-09-22: adding three import lines to src/lib/research-os/db.ts moved five entries, and removing five lines from read-access.ts moved a sixth. The repair a contributor reaches for is bumping the numbers, which is how six false reasons entered a sibling list: the reason travels to whatever read now sits on that line. Fix: key on an anchor of the form file::function::table::boundName::ordinal, the scheme the error allowlist already uses, and have the scan resolve an anchor to a line for reporting only. Verify by moving a read and confirming its entry still matches.

A power analysis computes naive and cluster-corrected per-arm n at three assumed effect sizes (d = 0.3/0.4/0.5, sourced to RESEARCH-OS-K12-SYSTEM-REVIEW.md section 9 and 04-compliance-distribution.md section 10) and three illustrative ICC values, finding Phase 1 underpowered for a confirmatory H1 test and registering it as a feasibility and effect-size-estimation pilot, with the fully powered target held for a Phase 2 extension of this same registration. The OSF template section order is sourced to van 't Veer and Giner-Sorolla (2016) after nine WebFetch attempts against osf.io returned no scrapeable template text (client-rendered SPA, 404s, a paywalled publisher redirect); the draft states this gap and instructs a live-form cross-check before any real submission. INSTRUMENTS.md: a retention probe schedule (immediate, 1 week, 8 weeks) reusing probe.ts's due-ness and grading pattern against the transfer task bank's sealed pool rather than repurposing the cold-start-only probeDue trigger; a metacognitive confidence item after every Check result plus an unrelated-topic confidence probe adapting Fisher, Goddu, and Keil (2015); a teacher time-on-review log operationalizing 04-compliance-distribution.md section 11's net-save-time adoption bar as a measured outcome. IRB-PACKET-OUTLINE.md: submission sections, consent and assent drafts for parents, under-13 students, 13-to-17 students, and teachers, a minimal-risk justification, a data-governance split between the operational FERPA school-official basis and the research consent track, and a founder-as-researcher conflict disclosure built on PLAN-REVISION-1.md section 5's two-PI pairing; states plainly that no IRB approval, partner PI, or partner school exists yet. description: Founder 2026-09-30: the main Bucket tool. One Next.js route, /explore, that runs canon search (src/app/api/canon/search, CanonGlobeMount) and advisor search (advisor-review.ts, prime-directions people file) through one query box and one shared scene. Views are modes on one scene engine: globe, helix, DNA, atom, particle, molecule, reaction, protein. Local first: localhost against the local stack, no hosted calls.
design:
Restart spec, founder 2026-09-30. It replaces design v1, which is kept in the bead history.

Shell. /explore uses the canon search shell unchanged: search, filters and sorts on the left or top center, and the right nav with full information and links. /canon/search itself does not change. The only new part is the center component: a full-page component centred in the available space.

Center component. One rendering framework for every data set: canon excerpts, advisors and every downloaded corpus.
1 Circle chart. A data set's fields map to the PCA or SVD circle chart of the prime-directions and advisor tools: spokes are components, and each observation is a polygon of its standardized scores. Sparse or non-numeric data, such as tokens, is integrated to fill the full distribution, so the circle can be smooth numerically. Averages across the data set's observations are drawn on the same chart.
2 Slices. The circle charts stack as slices in a locked higher view, left to right and back to front. Scrolling steps through them like a file system, and selecting one goes straight to its circle chart. A transparent cylinder encloses the stack.
3 Cylinder. The full cylinder is the slices joined into one smooth surface.
4 Sphere, and sphere through time: these already exist in the solvability atlas.
5 Helix. It shows events through time, or any circle chart swept along one variable such as time. Sequences show as a helix or as slices. The helicoid is for DNA.
6 3D polar plots, using radius, polar distance and charge, and experiments running through time.
Interaction: click to select. On a single circle chart, scrolling steps through its variable, such as advisor or time.

Basis: the canon search components plus both advisor tools (the prime-directions advisor page and the bkt desktop Advisors view), through one adapter. The existing renders to reuse: the prime-directions radar, and the solvability atlas SliceCircle, SolvabilitySpace, cylinder, sphere and helix (#442).
7 Stepper. Replace every list of item buttons (advisor names, event names, slice labels) with one drag scrubber: a thin track with a handle, plus the current item's label and index (for example "Lascaux cave paintings 1 / 260"). Dragging the handle and scrolling both move it. In every view, including the globe and sphere views, when there is a variable to step such as time, scroll steps it. Scroll never changes the size, zoom or orientation of the globe.
8 Home globe. Everything the home page globe at / does is folded into /explore: its scrubber, events, markers and interactions.
9 Full screen. As on the home page, the main component expands to full screen. It sits underneath the nav bars and the other components, and in full screen the search, filters, scrubber and right nav float on top of it or inside it as rounded-corner widgets. An exit control, plus Esc, returns to the normal layout. Build the controls as widgets on a base layer, so more widgets can be added later.
10 Data switcher. A control lists every available data set: canon, advisors, each local corpus, the Drive canon and anything uploaded. Picking one swaps the data in the current view, and the view, zoom and orientation stay put. The choice is kept in the URL as ?data=.

description:
graph.import_files records an object in the research-os-imports bucket, and the two live on opposite sides of a boundary no foreign key crosses. An owner may delete the object under research_os_imports_own_delete while the row survives naming a path that resolves to nothing, and a consumer cannot tell that from a path that never existed. Deleting the account cascades the row away and leaves the bytes, because storage.objects references only storage.buckets, so an object stays with an owner uuid pointing at a user who no longer exists. Fix: a delete route that removes the object and marks the row in one call, a tombstone column so a run that recorded the input can say what happened, and account deletion that clears the objects before the cascade.

description:
scripts/research-os/graph-keys.ts declares every non-partial unique key in the graph schema and orderIsTotal checks an order against it. Partial indexes are left out, because a key that holds only under a predicate makes an order total only when the read pins that predicate to the value the predicate names. graph.evidence_source_admissions carries a unique (source_id, scope) where status = 'active', and quotableRevisions in src/lib/research-os/evidence-search/server.ts pins both scope and status='active', so that read is total under the partial key and the gate cannot see it. The read now carries the full key and costs one sort column, so nothing is broken. Fix when a second read needs it: record each partial key with its predicate column and required value, and count it only when the read pins that column to that value with eq().

description: Founder 2026-09-27 ideal state. Same task set scored three ways: human alone, AI alone, human with AI. The gap is a per-person HAI multiplier tracked over time next to the grip sphere. Spec: _intake/ideas/IDEAL-STATE-2026-09-27.md.
design:
Home: packages/bkt (offline TUI, WAL SQLite, AES-GCM columns). New mode: bkt hai. Rev 3.

Frozen bank: buildQuestion draws distractors per seed and the 998-item pack stores no choices. A one-time step freezes 3 distractors per item (seeded buildQuestion, then stored) into hai_bank(item_id, stem, choices[4], answer, tier, pack_version). hai mode shows only frozen questions, shuffling display order alone. A is scored on that exact frozen question, making it an item property.

Probe: 40 unseen bank items in 20 pairs matched on tier and AI correctness; a seeded coin sends one of each pair to solo (H), one to paired (J). Guess-corrected score s = (c - 1/4) / (3/4).

A, AI alone: Batches API, claude-opus-5-5, effort low, one run (no temperature on this model). Answer and one-line rationale are frozen with model id and date. About $14 for 998 items, $7 batched; a 200-item pilot measures usage first (~$0.70). Probe A = mean s of the AI on its J items.

Pair: on J items a 20 s solo window, then the frozen AI answer and rationale; accept or override; accepted_ai stored.

Feedback policy: no correctness shown on any hai item until its retest ends, and hai items never enter FSRS review. Between t and t+7d the only exposure is the AI answer on J items, so retention (H items) and learning (J items) stay separate. Scores and answers appear after the retest.

Retest at t+7d, unaided, all 40:
- R = s(H items, t+7d) - s(H, t)
- L = s(J items, t+7d) - s(H, t), with matched halves
- Dependence flag when the 95% CI of J - H lies above 0 and the CI of L includes or lies below 0.

Metrics: primary D = J - max(H, A). Secondary is the founder ratio m = J / max(H, A), shown beside D and null when the max < 0.1. Bootstrap over matched pairs (resample pairs, keep both items) for every CI.

Precision: on the guess-corrected scale at p = 0.5, a 95% CI half-width of 0.10 on J - H needs about 340 items per condition (50% chance to exclude 0 at a true 0.10); 80% needs about 680. A half-width of 0.15 needs about 150. The 998-item bank caps one person at 499 per condition, so the target is half-width 0.10 after 17 probes, and every number on screen shows n and its CI. No trend line before 5 probe-plus-retest pairs (200 items).

description: Founder 2026-09-27 ideal state. Axes are root foundations or canon branches; each radius is mastered depth from foundation toward frontier; volume is one grip score shown on the profile with the prerequisites still missing. Spec: _intake/ideas/IDEAL-STATE-2026-09-27.md.
design:
DATA SOURCE: Offline EngineState lives in browser localStorage under bucket-academy/v1/<branch>, read and written by src/lib/academy/progress-store.ts (readLocal, writeLocal, localBranches). No separate native app store exists in this repo. Signed-in users merge it with /api/academy/progress (mergeState in engine.ts). Per-atom mastery comes from masteryFor in engine.ts, fused M = proficiency^a * retention^b (mastery.ts fuseMastery).

CURRENT AND PEAK: Retention decays, so each branch reports two values. Current = fused mastery now. Peak = proficiency with retention held at 1 (what the user reached before forgetting). The UI shows current as the solid vector and peak as a faint outline; the gap is what review would restore.

GEOMETRY: Canons sit on a circle. Each branch takes its angle from the circle layout on dev (circleProjection in src/components/canon-globe/projections.ts, branch sort in buildThetaIndex, 9 entries in BRANCH_ORDER). Each branch vector points out at its angle with length = that branch mean mastery. In the math every branch is its own basis vector in R^9, so branches are mutually perpendicular there; the angle level between two branches is 90 degrees in R^9 and 360/9 degrees on the circle. The 3D and 2D views are projections, and the view labels them as distorting angles.

RADIUS: r = equal-weight mean of the branch masteries, the headline grip number. The atom-weighted mean shows beside it as a secondary value.

WHAT THE USER SEES: On /canon circle view, a "My grip" toggle draws the branch vectors in branch colors and a ring or translucent sphere of radius r. Hover a vector: branch, current, peak, atoms mastered out of total.

PRIVACY: Computed on the device from the viewer own state. Nothing new is sent. No cross-user aggregate; that consent stays with bkt-jz4r.

TESTS: scripts/test-grip-sphere.ts: empty state gives r=0; all mastered gives r=1; r equals the branch-equal mean; atom-weighted mean differs when branch sizes differ; peak >= current; branch angles match the circle layout; output is deterministic.

SLICE 1: pure src/lib/academy/grip-sphere.ts with its test, plus the grip number and per-branch current and peak bars on the Learn page from localStorage.
notes: Founder 2026-09-29: Map the canons on a circle; vectors point out at perpendicular angle levels; sphere radius = average mastery across all tokens or canon.

description:
src/app/research-os/(app)/workspace/EvidenceFind.tsx has no effect on branch or targetNodeId, and the workspace renders it without a key, so the component stays mounted while `selected` changes. A learner searches on one step, clicks another step in the path, and the cards found for the first step stay on screen under the second. Quote would attach a source to a target it was never about, which is the provenance confusion the receipt contract exists to prevent. IMPLEMENTATION.md, UI behavior, asks for late responses to be ignored after a newer query or target change, and for no stale cards to look like the current answer. Fixed on fix/ros-find-target-change: an effect on [branch, targetNodeId] aborts the request in flight, moves the sequence so a late answer is dropped, and clears the cards. Covered by tests/e2e/evidence-search.spec.ts, which fails without the effect.

description:
Founder idea 2026-09-18, carries ros-25. Decompose any node (a concept, a law, an equation) into its factors, ask of each factor whether it decomposes further, and stop at primes that do not. The equals sign is the worked example of a prime that many nodes contain. The prime signature of a node, the penetration of each prime, and the tier follow from the dependency graph. A node built from many uncertain factors is less likely to hold, so a truth level propagates from primes through factors with statistical network methods: noisy-AND with shared-factor dependence, PageRank, betweenness, k-core, articulation points, bootstrap intervals. Slices: 1 decomposition, signature, penetration, tier, and the PRIMES.md memo over the local graph; 2 the decompose-further queue with model-proposed factors held for review; 3 the truth level and network statistics; 4 the node page made-of section and map layers.

description:
scripts/check-code-citations.mjs matches CITE = /path:(\d+)/, so a document naming a file with no line number is never resolved and the run reports 'every citation resolves'. Two documents named src/lib/research-os/import-storage.ts and supabase/migrations/20260922020000_research_os_import_files.sql, neither of which exists at that revision, under a sentence saying storage was built; the checker passed both. Adding a bare-path pass is four lines and finds 711 citations across the repo that resolve to nothing: 268 in learning/research-os/CHANGE-LEDGER.md, 62 in SOFTWARE-ATLAS.md, 36 in docs/PROBLEM-REGISTER.md, and a long tail. Not all are defects. A change ledger records what a path was, so naming a file that has since moved is its job, and the sample includes alias forms like @/data/world-indicators.js that the suffix resolver cannot follow. The work is the triage rather than the check: decide which trees the rule covers, teach the resolver the @/ alias, give a ledger an exemption marker, then turn it on. Shipping the check without that means writing 711 exemptions in a hurry, which is how six false reasons entered the paging allowlist.

The unprimed agent completed discover->query->cite with ZERO objection to the payment/citation mechanism (bkt-2 effectively PASS; verified raw served content has no injection — the subagent's FAIL verdict was rubric-artifact + it misattributed its own MCP system-context as fetched content). description:
graph.import_quota_gate refuses a write past 500 objects or 2 GiB for one owner in the research-os-imports bucket. Those two numbers were chosen so that a bound exists, and nobody has decided what a learner should be allowed to hold. They live in the migration as literals in the trigger body. 2 GiB at the 50 MiB per-object limit is about 40 full-size files or 500 small ones. The shape of the decision: what a learner holds, whether staff or a class hold more, whether the bound is per owner or per class, and what a person sees when they reach it. The mechanism is correct whatever the numbers are, since the gate locks the owner's row and counts every object and every byte, so changing them is editing two literals and re-running the migration. Until then an owner at the limit sees the Postgres check_violation message through the import page, which feat/ros-import-upload turns into a sentence about finishing or removing files.

description:
Three checks shipped in one day could not fire on some input, and none of the three was found by a run of the check. SEALED asserted over two sets that are disjoint by construction, so the assertion could never fail. The paging rule matched column and table names with [a-z_]+, so a table whose name carries a digit never matched and its paged read left the rule without failing it. The parse-order rule tested each following statement's whole subtree text, so an ok check on any other response answered for the parse under test. The loud direction costs an hour. The silent direction costs nothing visible: the rule looks like coverage and is absent on the rows it cannot see, and no run reports that. Give each structural gate a case that fails when the gate narrows, in the gate's own file, next to the rule it guards. Three now carry one: paging-discipline pins the column-name class, error-scan pins the refusal arm against two empty shapes, and the render rule carries its defect plus three negative controls. The rest do not.

description: Founder 2026-09-28. Bucket needs educational grant funding, which mostly requires 501(c)(3) status or a fiscal sponsor. Use nonprofit-application/ (reinstatement packet), compare filing against a fiscal sponsor for speed, and list education grants Bucket can apply to now. Grant drafts go through the Longtail chisel queue.
design:
## Legal Path
nonprofit-application/ is a draft: no entity, EIN, sponsor or filing. Bridge: comprehensive (Model A) fiscal sponsorship. The sponsor's board owns the assets, holds variance power and approves every grant; Bucket recommends. Plan on full Form 1023, since pass-through gifts likely exceed the 1023-EZ $50K cap. Donors can direct gifts to a topic fund; gifts earmarked for a named person fail deductibility (Pub. 526, https://www.irs.gov/publications/p526). No donor-advised fund (IRC 4966).
Sponsor fit, each to confirm in writing, including whether it pays grants to individual researchers:
- Players Philanthropy Fund, research and education, $5K deposit: https://www.ppf.org/
- Community Initiatives, broad charitable: https://communityin.org/
- Code for Science & Society, open research software: https://www.codeforsociety.org/
- Hack Club Bank, 7%: https://hackclub.com/fiscal-sponsorship/
Fractured Atlas takes arts projects only. Open Collective Foundation closed in 2024.
State registration: the sponsor registers for charitable solicitation.

## Donor Flow
Topic funds, one per canon branch (01-mathematics to 07-mind), each with open selection, plus a General Fund. A magazine issue links to its branch fund. Donor copy describes the use of funds and the selection process, with no impact claims. The sponsor issues receipts under IRC 170(f)(8) (Pub. 1771, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1771.pdf).

## Conflict of Interest
- Founder recuses from any grant to himself, family, AGFarms or related parties (05-CONFLICT-OF-INTEREST-POLICY.md).
- An independent panel of at least 3 people with no ties to Bucket scores applications; the sponsor approves.
- Written criteria are published before any solicitation (https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/private-foundations/grants-to-individuals).
- The founder assigns domain, code and wallet to the sponsor, later the entity.

## Reaching Researchers
Open call per fund, published rubric, signed grant agreement with a use restriction and a report-back. University researchers are paid through their institution.

## Impact Reporting
Internal allocation uses the expected-discovery objective (_intake/ideas/EXPECTED-DISCOVERY-OBJECTIVE-THEORY.md) and the education model (reports/Bucket education market and impact.md). Quarterly public report per fund: dollars in, grants out, outputs.

## Cost-Effectiveness
Internal, GiveWell-style explicit models with skeptical adjustment (https://www.givewell.org/how-we-work/our-criteria/cost-effectiveness/cost-effectiveness-models). 80,000 Hours scale, neglectedness and tractability decide which funds open (https://80000hours.org/articles/problem-framework/). Named uncertainty: no track record, subjective discovery counts, unknown counterfactual. Publish ranges after a year of data.

## x402 and Payments
Donations run on Stripe through the sponsor on a ledger kept apart from citation fees. LAWYER: private-benefit risk of citation-fee payments to authors (founder included), unrelated business income, crypto gift acceptance and Form 8283, sponsor agreement, fund language.

## First Slice
1. Weeks 0-2: apply to PPF and CS&S; HCB as fallback. Budget 5-10% fee, PPF $5K deposit.
2. Weeks 2-4: publish CRITERIA.md (eligibility, rubric, panel names, recusal rule); recruit the panel.
3. Weeks 4-12: on signing, assign assets, open General Fund plus 05-biophysics fund.
4. Pilot: $5K, two $2.5K grants by open call, panel-scored, sponsor-approved, public report.

description:
supabase/migrations/20260915000000_research_os_access.sql:102 writes `select 1 from graph.node_grants g where g.node_id = id and g.grantee_id = auth.uid()`. In that scope `id` binds to node_grants.id, so the live policy body reads `g.node_id = g.id`: it compares a grant's own primary key to the node the grant is for. Confirmed against the local catalog with `select qual from pg_policies where tablename='nodes' and policyname='visible_select'`. The clause can never match, so a grantee has never been admitted by row-level security on graph.nodes, and only public nodes and the owner's own are visible under it. Latent rather than live: `authenticated` holds no USAGE on schema graph, so no client reaches the policy and every read goes through a service-role route that applies read-access.ts instead. It becomes live the day schema usage is granted. Fix: a new migration that recreates the policy with `g.node_id = nodes.id`, plus a fixture that inserts a grant and asserts the grantee reads the node under `set local role authenticated`. Do not edit the 20260915 file, which is already applied.

design:
Graph source: prerequisite edges in the academy graph (graph.learning_items and its edge table, 820 edges over 487 nodes from academy-import; canon prereqs via prereq_ancestor). The Lean result assumes an exact graph, so the planner uses reviewed/confirmed prerequisite edges only. Pending or low-confidence edges show as "suggested" and leave the order unchanged. Exactness is a data claim: the UI says "minimal for the reviewed graph" and reports unreviewed foundations as a typed warning.

Algorithm (src/lib/academy/prereq-path.ts, pure TS): target t, edges E, mastered set M. (1) C(t) = t plus all ancestors by reverse DFS. (2) M_C = M intersect C(t); check the target-local predicate (every mastered node in C(t) has its immediate prereqs in M). A violation returns a typed MasteryConflict. (3) Emit C(t) minus M_C in topological order (Kahn, ties by tier then id). Typed failures: Cycle, MissingNode, MasteryConflict, UnreviewedFoundation. Matches Learning.lean: RestrictedKnown, remaining_necessary, minimum_unit_distance. Unit cost only; weighted effort is out of scope.

Mastery: mastered = fused mastery threshold from src/lib/academy/mastery.ts (the one rollupBranch uses) over engine state from progress-store readLocal, merged with server progress when online. Offline, the graph comes from the bundled corpus (corpus.ts), so the bkt app plans with no network.

UI: Learn gets a "Path to" concept picker (search over atoms). The page shows the ordered list, mastered ancestors collapsed as done, the remaining step count, and a Start button that opens StudySession on the first ready node. Conflicts render as a banner naming the nodes.

Tests: scripts/test-academy-prereq-path.ts. Fixtures from evaluate.py: diamond with disconnected node, shortcut, mastered target, unmastered foundation, disjoint 4->5 edge. Property test: port the exhaustive generator (n<=5, 1,099 DAGs, downward-closed mastery, 57,060 cases) and assert zero distance error against an independent BFS over knowledge states, plus: output is topological, every node is required, every node is ready when reached. One test per typed failure. Corpus test: the real 487-node graph has no cycles and plans every target.

First slice: prereq-path.ts plus the property test, then a read-only /learn/path?to=<atom> page on local mastery. Start button and server merge follow.
title: Learn: backward prerequisite path from any frontier concept

Calibration record: learnerConfidence, sourcePrediction, predictionCorrect land in the evidence jsonb per an updated EVIDENCE-SCHEMA.md; calibration.ts's computeCalibrationSummary (mean confidence against mean source-prediction correctness, forcing-gated check events only) is wired into GET /api/research-os/class and rendered on /research-os/class, confirmed untouched by other in-flight work via git log -3 --since='2 hours ago' -- src/app/research-os/class before adding it directly rather than leaving it as an unexposed server function. design:
# Marketing corpus plan

Base: origin/dev 09cfa401f. Branch feat/ros-marketing-corpus, PR into dev. Covers bkt-ixi6.

## Outcome

Scope for this PR: staff-only web page on a local-first install (the launch gate `staffOnlyAtLaunch` stays on) plus `bkt analyze` run from a source checkout. The packaged desktop binary gains the marketing section only after bead bkt-lheg bundles `analyze/marketing/` (it touches `packages/bkt/src/pack/pysrc.ts`, reserved for the platform agents, and lands after #429). Hosted Vercel answers 503 `analysis_local_only`. Desktop jobs support waits on PR #429 and is a filed bead.

A signed-in Research OS user drops an ad-platform export or any table file on /research-os/import/marketing, gets a marketing report (funnel metrics, CAC, LTV, cohorts, channel mix, attribution, trend, seasonality, anomalies), and can delete the file and every derived row. The same file passed to `bkt analyze` from a source checkout produces the same marketing section from the same Python code.

## One analysis core

New package `packages/bkt/analyze/marketing/`. Required deps: stdlib plus numpy (already in requirements.txt). Optional: `pypdf==6.10.2` for PDF and `pyarrow` (pinned to the version the Parquet fixture was made with) for Parquet, both added to requirements.txt; a missing optional dep fails that format with a named error code. This PR does not edit `packages/bkt/src`; bundling is bead bkt-lheg.

- `readers.py`: XLSX and PDF table readers that return (header, rows) for `bkt_analyze.read_table`, which gains `.xlsx` and `.pdf` branches. CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL and Parquet stay as they are.
- `adapters.py`: header fingerprints and column maps per platform.
- `schema.py`: the canonical record and the normalizer.
- `metrics.py`: every metric below.
- `bounded.py`: sets OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1, RLIMIT_AS 2 GiB, RLIMIT_CPU 90 s, RLIMIT_FSIZE 64 MB and RLIMIT_NOFILE 64, then runs `bkt_analyze.main`. Every web analysis runs through it, so XLSX, Parquet, delimited and PDF parsing all sit under one resource cap. The route adds a 120 s wall clock and kills the process group on expiry. The 2 GiB figure is measured: `small.parquet` fails `verify` under RLIMIT_AS 1 GiB and passes under 2 GiB with one BLAS thread [empirical: tests/fixtures/small.parquet, 2026-09-30, python3 with resource.setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS) then bkt_analyze.verify]. The PDF worker is its own process with its own RLIMIT_AS 1 GiB and RLIMIT_CPU 60 s; CPU time is counted per process, so it does not draw on the parent's 90 s. Tests run a Parquet, an XLSX and a PDF fixture through `bounded.py`.
- `report.py`: JSON section `marketing` plus Markdown `## Marketing`.

`bkt_analyze.py` takes one or more files (`bkt analyze a.csv b.xlsx`, at most 8) and calls `marketing.run(tables)` after the form check whenever an adapter or the generic entity detector matches, and adds `--marketing auto|on|off` (default auto). Report schema stays `bucket.analysis/1` with an additive `marketing` key, so the desktop analyze view and the jobs view keep rendering.

Web runs the same file: route `POST /api/research-os/marketing` downloads the import's objects with the service role into a 0700 temp dir and spawns `python3 packages/bkt/analyze/marketing/bounded.py <files...> --no-helix --marketing on --out <tmpdir>` under the local-first setup. Concurrency: at most 2 analyses at once per server process (503 `busy` beyond), one per owner at a time, and 20 per owner per hour (429 `rate_limited`); in-memory counters kept on `globalThis` so a dev-server hot reload keeps them; they suit the single-process local server and are named as such. `BKT_ANALYZE_PYTHON` names the interpreter; unset (Vercel) returns 503 `analysis_local_only` with copy that points to the desktop app. One code path, two callers; a parity test runs every fixture through both the CLI and the route handler and compares the `marketing` JSON.

## Formats

- Row cap: every reader stops at `--max-rows` (default 1,000,000) and sets `truncated`; the cap is enforced while reading. Decoding: UTF-8 with or without BOM, and UTF-16 when a UTF-16 BOM is present (Google Ads exports TSV as UTF-16).
- Numbers: currency symbols ($, EUR sign, GBP sign, and ISO codes as prefix or suffix) are stripped and recorded as the column currency; `1,234.56` and `1.234,56` are both read, chosen per column by which pattern at least 95% of values fit; a column that fits neither stays text and raises `W_NUMBER_FORMAT`. Percent columns (`12.5%`) are stored as fractions.
- Dates: ISO dates and datetimes, `Jan 5, 2026` (Google Ads), `2026-01-05 13:02:11 -0500` (Shopify), `2026-01-05 13:02` UTC (Stripe). A timestamp with an offset converts to its UTC day; a naive timestamp keeps its written day. The report states the rule.
- XLSX: stdlib `zipfile` plus `xml.etree` reader of the first worksheet (or `--sheet N`). Reads cached `<v>` values and shared strings only; `<f>` elements are ignored, so no formula runs and a formula cell with no cached value reads as missing and raises `W_FORMULA_UNCACHED`. Guards before parsing: magic `PK\x03\x04`, `[Content_Types].xml` present with the spreadsheetml main type, at most 2,000 zip members; each member is read through a counting stream that stops at 64 MB and the whole archive at 200 MB whatever the headers declare; no DOCTYPE in any parsed part (rejects entity expansion), macro-enabled parts (`vbaProject.bin`) rejected with `E_XLSX_MACRO`. Dates from serials use the 1900 system, or 1904 when `workbookPr date1904` is set. Cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` keep their text and are tagged in the report; nothing re-exports them to a spreadsheet.
- PDF tables: worker subprocess `marketing/pdfworker.py`, its own copy of the pattern in `prime_directions/pdfworker.py` plus `fitme._bounded` (PR #390, merged): pypdf `extract_text(extraction_mode="layout")`, 40 pages, 60 s wall, RLIMIT_AS 1 GiB, pypdf decompression caps of 50 MB set in the worker. It imports nothing from `prime_directions`, so the desktop bundle needs no extra package. Lines split into cells on runs of 2+ spaces; the header is the first line whose cell count equals the modal count; rows with other counts are dropped and counted in `W_PDF_ROWS_DROPPED`. Scanned PDFs with no text layer fail with `E_PDF_NO_TEXT`. Accuracy is empirical and measured on the fixtures only; the report says so.

## Adapters

Each adapter has `required` header tokens (all must appear after normalization: lowercase, currency suffix stripped, punctuation collapsed), `optional` tokens, and a column map into the canonical schema. Score = matched required plus 0.25 per optional; highest score wins, ties go to the generic detector. Preamble handling: skip leading `#` lines (GA4) and search the first 15 rows for the header (Google Ads title rows).

| Platform | Required fingerprint | Grain |
|---|---|---|
| Meta Ads | campaign name, amount spent, impressions, reporting starts; optional purchases, purchases conversion value | ad facts |
| Google Ads | campaign, cost, impr., clicks; optional conversions, conv. value | ad facts |
| GA4 | session default channel group or first user default channel group, sessions | traffic facts |
| Shopify orders | name, financial status, total, created at | transactions |
| Stripe payments | id, amount, created date (utc), status | transactions |
| HubSpot deals | record id, deal stage, amount, close date | transactions |

Joins across files: one analysis takes up to 8 files from one import. Ad-grain files give spend, impressions, clicks and platform-reported conversions and value by day and channel. Transaction files give orders, customers and revenue by day, and a channel when the file has one (HubSpot original source, Shopify referring site or UTM source when present). Channel names map through a fixed table (facebook, instagram and meta to `paid_social_meta`; google, adwords and cpc to `paid_search_google`; others to their lowercased name). Blended CAC and blended ROAS use total spend over the shared date range against transaction revenue and new customers in that range; per-channel ROAS uses platform-reported value when present and joined transaction revenue by channel otherwise, each labelled with its source. Metrics that lack their inputs return null with a reason naming the missing file type.

Fixtures: one synthetic export per platform under `packages/bkt/analyze/tests/fixtures/marketing/`, generated by `make_marketing_fixtures.py` from a fixed seed, with invented campaign names, `example.com` emails and `cus_test_` ids. No real customer data. Each fixture has an expected-output JSON checked by test, and the pair Meta plus Shopify has non-null CAC, ROAS and LTV in its expected output. XLSX and PDF fixtures are generated from the same seed (XLSX written by the stdlib writer in the fixture script; PDF written by a minimal PDF text writer in the script, so no new dependency).

## Canonical schema

`marketing.v1` record: `date` (ISO day), `platform`, `channel`, `campaign`, `spend`, `currency`, `impressions`, `clicks`, `sessions`, `conversions`, `revenue`, `customer_id`, `order_id`, `status`. Two grains: `ad` rows (date x campaign facts) and `txn` rows (one per order or payment). Refunded, failed and canceled statuses are excluded from revenue and counted. Currency: a single currency per file is required for money metrics; mixed currencies raise `W_MIXED_CURRENCY` and money metrics are reported per currency with no conversion. Customer ids are hashed with a per-run random salt before they enter the report, so the report carries no raw email or id.

## Metrics

Definitions become Lean in a new module `lean/BucketMath/Marketing.lean` over `Rat`, added to the manifest by `bm.py check --write`. Division by zero returns null with a reason.

| Metric | Formula | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| CTR | clicks / impressions | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.ctr], bounded by [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.ctr_le_one] when clicks <= impressions |
| CPC | spend / clicks | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cpc] |
| CPA | spend / conversions | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cpa], [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cpa_mul] (CPA x conversions = spend) |
| ROAS | revenue / spend | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.roas], [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.roas_ge_one_iff] |
| CAC | spend in period / new customers first seen in period | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cac] |
| LTV | mean revenue per customer over the observed window, historical only | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.ltv_hist]; no predictive LTV, the report states the window |
| Cohorts | customers grouped by first-order month; retention = share with an order in month k | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.retention_le_one] |
| Channel mix | channel spend / total spend | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.mix_sum_one] |
| Attribution | last-touch and linear over the channel column present in the file; no path data means last-touch by row channel | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.last_touch_conserves], [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.linear_conserves] |
| Trend | OLS slope on daily totals, reusing `trend_season` | [bm:BucketMath.Project.pythagoras_orthonormal] for the residual split |
| Seasonality | ACF peak on residuals, reusing `find_season`; weekday profile when >= 28 days | [empirical: 2/sqrt(n) white-noise bound from Box and Jenkins 1976, a chosen parameter; fixture recovery measured 2026-09-30, `pytest packages/bkt/analyze/tests/test_marketing.py -k season`] |
| Anomalies | median-MAD z on daily totals: abs(x - median) / (1.4826 x MAD) > 3.5 | [empirical: cutoff from Iglewicz and Hoaglin 1993, a chosen parameter; spike recall and flat-series silence measured 2026-09-30, `pytest packages/bkt/analyze/tests/test_marketing.py -k anomaly`] |

No causal claims. Attribution is labelled a heuristic. `bm.py check` certifies the Rat definitions and theorems only. The Python float code is tied to them by a differential test that recomputes every ratio metric on every fixture with `fractions.Fraction` and asserts agreement within 1e-9 relative, and asserts null exactly where the Lean `ratio` returns none.

## Storage and privacy

- Upload reuses the existing import storage path and page code: browser hashes, uploads to private bucket `research-os-imports` under `<owner>/<sha256>`, `POST /api/research-os/import` verifies bytes and records `graph.import_files`. The quota trigger caps 500 objects and 2 GiB per owner. Privacy per user: the marketing route creates its imports itself with `node_id` null (kind `dataset`, `source.marketing = true`), so `graph.can_read_import_object`, which joins through `graph.nodes`, admits no grantee and no public reader. The storage key is `<owner>/<sha256>`, shared by any import of the same bytes; if that path is also recorded under an import whose node is public or granted, the route refuses with 409 `object_shared` and names the other import. SQL test: a grantee of an unrelated node cannot read a marketing object, and anon cannot. Later attach: the existing `POST /api/research-os/import` attach action refuses with 409 `object_marketing` when the same storage path is recorded under a marketing import, so the symmetry holds in both orders; a vitest case covers attach after marketing.
- Size: the bucket takes 50 MB; marketing analysis caps each file at 16 MB (the desktop jobs cap) and 64 MB per analysis, checked from the recorded bytes before download, and 1,000,000 rows, enforced inside the readers.
- Upload checks, client and server: extension allowlist (csv, tsv, xlsx, json, jsonl, parquet, pdf), declared MIME normalized, and server-side magic bytes on the stored object (`PK\x03\x04` for xlsx, `%PDF-` for pdf, `PAR1` for parquet, UTF-8 decodable and no NUL in the first 64 KB for text). Mismatch returns 415 and nothing runs.
- Encryption at rest: the raw object relies on storage-layer encryption (hosted Supabase encrypts storage at rest; the local stack relies on an encrypted host disk, stated in docs/AUTH.md and unverified by code). Derived output is sealed in the app layer. DDL:

```
graph.marketing_reports (
  id uuid pk default gen_random_uuid(),
  import_id uuid not null references graph.imports(id) on delete cascade,
  owner_id uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  input_digest text not null,        -- sha256 over the sorted file sha256 list
  analyzer_version text not null,    -- pysrc version hash
  key_id text not null,
  iv bytea not null, ciphertext bytea not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (import_id, input_digest, analyzer_version)
)
```

RLS on, no policy, service role only, revoked from anon and authenticated. AES-256-GCM, key from HKDF-SHA256 over the key named by `key_id` with the owner id as info, random 96-bit IV, AAD = owner id, import id, input digest. Keys come from `MARKETING_SEAL_KEYS` (`id:base64,...`, first is current); rotation adds a key at the front and old rows keep decrypting. Insert uses `on conflict do nothing` then reads the row, so a double click or retry returns the same report. `GET /api/research-os/marketing?import=<id>` decrypts and returns the saved report. Missing or malformed key config: POST and GET fail closed with 503 `seal_key_missing` before any analysis runs.
- Delete on request: `DELETE /api/research-os/marketing?import=<id>` removes each storage object of that import that no other `graph.import_files` row names, the `graph.imports` row (cascading `import_files` and `marketing_reports`), and returns counts. Storage removal failure returns 502 and leaves rows so a retry can finish. Account deletion cascades through `auth.users`.
- No third parties: the route spawns local Python only; no fetch to any host. A test asserts the route module imports no HTTP client and the Python package imports no network module.
- No logging of uploads: route errors log the error code only, never file names, cell values or report content; the route never forwards Python stderr. In marketing mode the Python side catches every exception at the top and prints one error code; temp dirs are 0700 and removed in `finally`. Test: a failing parse of a file holding a marker string leaves the marker out of captured console output and stderr.
- Output escaping: the web report renders through React text nodes only, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; the Markdown report escapes `|`, backticks, `<`, `>` and `[` in user values. Test: a campaign named `<script>alert(1)</script>` and a cell `=HYPERLINK("x")` come out inert in both.
- Retention: storage deletion is immediate. Hosted Supabase backups keep deleted rows and objects until the backup window expires (the plan's tier sets it); the local stack keeps no backups. The page states both.
- Desktop: `bkt analyze` keeps writing to the 0700 analyses directory. Desktop at-rest encryption of saved reports is out of scope (packages/bkt/src is owned by another agent) and filed as a bead.

## Surfaces

- Web: `src/app/research-os/(app)/import/marketing/page.tsx` (staff-only at launch) reuses the import page's hashing, upload and attach helpers (extracted to `src/lib/research-os/import-client.ts`, the import page switches to it with no behavior change), then calls the marketing route and renders the report with a delete button. Behind `staffOnlyAtLaunch` like the import route.
- Desktop: `bkt analyze file.xlsx` works through the Python core with no TS change. The desktop jobs input allowlist (`job-specs.ts`, owned by PR #429) needs `.xlsx`, `.parquet`, `.pdf` added; filed as a bead for after #429 merges.
- bkt-ui Import view: unchanged in this PR; a bead covers linking it to the analyze job once the allowlist lands.

## Tests

- Python `tests/test_marketing.py`: locale numbers, UTF-16 BOM, offset timestamps, lying zip headers caught by the counting stream, row cap truncation, Fraction differential, escaping, the Meta plus Shopify join; each adapter fixture detects the right platform and matches expected metrics; XLSX formula cell yields cached value and never evaluates; zip bomb, macro workbook, DOCTYPE part, and wrong magic are rejected; PDF fixture parses to the expected table; zero-denominator metrics return null; cohort retention in [0, 1]; mix sums to 1 within 1e-9; attribution totals equal conversion totals; anomaly detector flags an injected spike and nothing on a flat series.
- TS vitest: magic-byte check, size caps, 429 and 503 under the limiter, timeout kill, 409 `object_shared`, shared-object survival on delete, idempotent re-POST, 503 `seal_key_missing`, key rotation decrypt, route auth (401 unauthenticated, 404 on another owner's import), 503 when `BKT_ANALYZE_PYTHON` unset, seal round trip and AAD mismatch failure, delete path including storage failure, no-network import assertion, parity with the CLI output.
- SQL test `supabase/tests/research_os_marketing_reports.sql`: RLS denies another owner, cascade on import delete.
- Lean: `bm.py check` passes with the new module.
- Existing suites: `packages/bkt/analyze/tests`, `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `tsc`.

## Rollout

Additive: one migration (`graph.marketing_reports`, service-role only, cascade), new route, new page, new Python modules. Staff-only at launch through the existing gate. Rollback: revert the PR and drop the table; no existing table changes.

## Deferred beads

Filed before the build with `needs-founder` and `source-agent`: bundle `analyze/marketing` in the desktop pysrc after #429 (bkt-lheg); desktop jobs allowlist and 16 MB cap after #429; desktop report encryption; Google Sheets link import; multi-touch paths from GA4 path exports; currency conversion; shared rate limiter for a multi-process host.

description: Founder 2026-09-30: the desktop app should include all of Research OS and the tools built so far, keeping only the efficient parts. Candidates: Learn with prerequisite path and grip sphere, quiz and review, work quiz, canon explorer (globe and circle), solvability atlas, bkt analyze with helix, human-AI multiplier, advisor review and fit-me (local people file), prime directions, workspace and notes, hypothesis engine via local hte-serve when present. Plan first: which parts run offline in the window, which stay CLI-only, size and memory budget, what is dropped as too heavy.
design:
Plan v2 2026-09-30, supersedes v1. Rule: the window runs a screen offline when its data is local and it needs no Supabase, pgvector or network. Heavy compute runs as host-Python jobs. Each ported screen reads /local/* over bkt.db, bundled JSON or a picked file handle.

Window, offline:
- Learn, prerequisite path, grip sphere, quiz, review: shipped.
- Work quiz: source is a picked .beads/issues.jsonl plus the local git log of a picked repo; tab hidden when neither is set.
- Canon globe and circle: bucket-canon pack (5.3 MB); three and react-three as a lazy chunk (~900 KB gz); one 2k texture (~1.5 MB).
- Solvability, software, patents, status: static JSON (0.3 MB).
- Human-AI multiplier: view over the existing HaiStore.
- Advisor review and prime directions: viewer for precomputed advisor-review and prime-direction JSON opened through a /local/pick handle.
- Workspace notes: notes, pins and state in bkt.db.
- History: local snapshot of the user's own productions.

Host-Python jobs, started from the window through a /local/jobs route:
- bkt analyze with helix (numpy).
- Fit-me and advisor review (TF-IDF plus randomized SVD: numpy, scipy, sklearn). pi-fit embeddings need sentence-transformers and stay optional; missing deps show an install hint. No TS port of pi-fit scoring.
- Hypothesis engine: tab shows only when hte-serve at 127.0.0.1:8420 answers /health; serve proxies it.

Dropped from the window: attend (vector search), class and home (multi-user), import (Supabase storage), nsm, roadmap, workbench.

People-file privacy: bkt.db keeps publishable rows only; emails, tracker notes and statement text stay in the picked file and are never copied. People tables are excluded from hub sync by a table allowlist. `bkt forget people` deletes them and writes a marker; a later import refuses rows the marker covers unless re-picked with confirmation.

Budget: AppImage 35 MB now, estimate 45 MB after the canon pack, texture and UI (~3 MB). Only a bundled Python runtime with numpy and scipy (~120 MB) or torch would pass 150 MB; neither ships. Memory: serve under 150 MB RSS, globe under 300 MB.

Navigation: sidebar groups Learn (Learn, Quiz, Review, Work quiz), Explore (Canon, Solvability, Software), Research (Advisor, Prime directions, Workspace, History, Multiplier), Jobs (Analyze, Fit-me, Hypotheses), Import.

Security: same serve auth, header token, Host and Origin checks, per-route body caps; files only through opaque /local/pick handles; jobs run a fixed allowlist of commands with argv arrays, never a shell string.

Slices:
2.0 Each reused screen splits into a pure view plus a data hook. A shared typed contract in src/lib/research-os/contract.ts, web and local adapters, contract tests run the same fixtures against /api/research-os and /local, plus web regression tests on the current pages.
2a Advisor review and prime-directions viewer, people privacy and forget.
2b Jobs route: analyze, fit-me, advisor review.
2c Static atlases, status, sidebar groups.
2d Canon circle, then globe lazy chunk, size gate check.
2e Work quiz from picked beads and git log, workspace notes, migration 4.
2f Multiplier view, history snapshot, hte-serve proxy.
notes: Mediums from plan v2 critic, folded into slices: 2b jobs run with a timeout, concurrency 1, cancellation, capped logs and marker-guarded output dirs. 2a forget markers store HMAC-keyed hashes (key in the device keyring), never raw names. 2a the viewer never displays or stores emails from a private-build file; email fields are dropped at parse.
title: Desktop app v0.3: Research OS and built tools in the window, offline and lightweight

description: Founder 2026-09-29. Any Bucket user uploads a research statement and CV as PDF; Research OS extracts text, embeds it as self phases, and renders the pi-fit charts and cards against every advisor. Extends bkt-o8xs.
design:
Local prototype, v2 2026-09-29, answers critic round 1. Scope: a local command, no server, no hosted DB, no network. The advisor path is TF-IDF plus truncated SVD from prime_directions, fitted on the people file; no model is downloaded.
1 Inputs: --statement (Markdown or text in slice 1; PDF in slice 2) and --cv (slice 2). PDF limits: 20 MB, 40 pages, 30 s per file; pypdf first with decompression capped, then pdftotext called as pdftotext -l 40 -- <path> -; a PDF that yields under 200 characters fails with 'this PDF has no text layer, export it with text or pass Markdown'.
2 People source: default is the public advisor export from bkt-abwh (advisor_public, emails stripped). --people overrides with a local file. Output is always built in publishable mode: no email from any source reaches --out.
3 Directions: parsed from a Research Directions section (numbered or bulleted items), else the top 6 statement paragraphs; --directions overrides.
4 Writes: only to --out. On creation the command writes --out/.bucket-fit-marker holding a random id and the version. It refuses an --out that exists, is non-empty and has no marker, and refuses a symlinked --out. --forget deletes --out only when the marker is present and --out is not a symlink, a filesystem root, the home directory or the repo; it deletes files inside --out and never follows symlinks. The page embeds the ranked rows, both stars and the statement-derived direction labels; it does not embed the statement or CV text. No telemetry.
5 Validation (slice 3): --validate pairs.csv (advisor OpenAlex id, student statement path, split year). Leakage control: works co-authored by the advisor and the student are excluded by author id, and advisor text is time-split to works before the split year. Baselines: unwhitened TF-IDF cosine, random order, h-index order. Reports MRR and recall@1, 10 and 100 with n. The report states that it measures topical retrieval of the known advisor and not advising fit.
6 The bkt desktop app wraps the command as 'bkt fit' after bkt-p3l4 Phase 1, in its own PR.
Slices: 1 Markdown or text statement, --people, --out, marker-guarded --forget, blocked-socket test. 2 PDF and CV. 3 --validate with baselines.
Tests slice 1: marker written; refuse unmarked non-empty and symlinked --out; --forget refuses home, root, repo and unmarked; no email in output with emails in input; directions parsing with and without a section; socket blocked during the run.
notes: Slices 1 and 2 merged (#389, #390). Slice 3 --validate waits on the founder choosing a source of 30 or more advisor-student pairs.
title: Upload research statement and CV PDF, plot yourself against every advisor
